meta.title: Paojilhuasca Integration Prompts
meta.description: 65 short prompts for post-retreat integration, each with a micro-practice. Categories: Body, Emotion, Social, Environment, Spirit, Milestone.
meta.author: Paojilhuasca (Fabrizio Beverina) & ChatGPT

prompts.prompt: Notice where your body feels alive today—what is it telling you?
prompts.practice: Place your hand there and breathe deeply 5 times.

prompts.prompt: What small movement could release tension right now?
prompts.practice: Stretch or shake your body gently for 1 minute.

prompts.prompt: How has your relationship with nourishment shifted since ceremony?
prompts.practice: Take one mindful sip of water or tea before writing.

prompts.prompt: Where do you feel gratitude in your body at this moment?
prompts.practice: Touch that area and whisper “thank you.”

prompts.prompt: What signals of healing does your body show you?
prompts.practice: Close your eyes and notice three subtle sensations.

prompts.prompt: How can you honor your body as the first doctor?
prompts.practice: Write your answer, then give yourself a gentle self-massage.

prompts.prompt: What new rhythms or cycles is your body asking you to follow?
prompts.practice: Place your hand on your belly and follow your breath for 1 minute.

prompts.prompt: Write about a time your body surprised you with strength or resilience.
prompts.practice: Stand tall, stretch your arms wide, and breathe in that memory.

prompts.prompt: What part of your body most needs your attention today?
prompts.practice: Breathe into that area, visualizing warmth flowing there.

prompts.prompt: How can you bring breath into the places that feel tight or closed?
prompts.practice: Inhale through the nose, exhale with a sigh 3 times.

prompts.prompt: In what ways has your sense of embodiment changed after medicine work?
prompts.practice: Walk slowly across the room, noticing each step.

prompts.prompt: What gesture of kindness can you offer your body today?
prompts.practice: Drink water slowly, savoring each sip as medicine.

prompts.prompt: Which emotion feels most present right now, and what does it want you to know?
prompts.practice: Name it aloud before journaling.

prompts.prompt: How has your understanding of fear changed after ceremony?
prompts.practice: Take one slow breath in, whisper “fear,” exhale with “release.”

prompts.prompt: What emotion feels unfinished and asks to be expressed?
prompts.practice: Scribble it on paper quickly before writing words.

prompts.prompt: Where have you discovered unexpected joy?
prompts.practice: Smile intentionally for 10 seconds before you write.

prompts.prompt: How does sadness flow through you when you let it move freely?
prompts.practice: Let out a gentle sigh or hum.

prompts.prompt: What emotion have you learned to welcome rather than resist?
prompts.practice: Open your palms face up, inviting it in.

prompts.prompt: Write about an emotion that connects you to your younger self.
prompts.practice: Place your hand on your heart and say, “I see you.”

prompts.prompt: Which feeling is teaching you patience today?
prompts.practice: Count 5 slow breaths before journaling.

prompts.prompt: What emotion would you like to give more space for in your life?
prompts.practice: Expand your chest as you inhale deeply.

prompts.prompt: How does love express itself differently in you now?
prompts.practice: Write one person’s name and send them silent blessings.

prompts.prompt: What emotion carries hidden wisdom for you?
prompts.practice: Close your eyes and imagine that emotion as a teacher.

prompts.prompt: How do you practice compassion toward your difficult feelings?
prompts.practice: Hold your own hand gently while journaling.

prompts.prompt: Who has supported your journey, and how can you thank them?
prompts.practice: Write a short message of gratitude after journaling.

prompts.prompt: What relationships feel more authentic after your experience?
prompts.practice: Smile as you picture their faces.

prompts.prompt: How do you wish to show up differently with others?
prompts.practice: Stand tall, shoulders back, and breathe.

prompts.prompt: Where do you sense more courage to speak your truth?
prompts.practice: Speak one sentence out loud to the empty room.

prompts.prompt: What community values are most important to you now?
prompts.practice: Write 3 values and circle the one that shines most.

prompts.prompt: Write about a recent conversation that felt like medicine.
prompts.practice: Close your eyes and replay one sentence from it.

prompts.prompt: How do you want to repair or nurture a relationship that matters?
prompts.practice: Place your hand on your heart and imagine them smiling.

prompts.prompt: What boundaries protect your newfound clarity?
prompts.practice: Draw a small circle on your page—your safe space.

prompts.prompt: How can you share your insights without needing others to agree?
prompts.practice: Whisper “My truth is enough.”

prompts.prompt: Which connection feels most nourishing at this moment?
prompts.practice: Write their name slowly and with care.

prompts.prompt: How has your sense of belonging changed?
prompts.practice: Recall one place where you felt fully accepted.

prompts.prompt: What new forms of service or contribution call to you?
prompts.practice: List one small act of service you can do this week.

prompts.prompt: How has your relationship with nature shifted since ceremony?
prompts.practice: Step outside or look out the window for 1 minute.

prompts.prompt: Write about a place in the natural world that feels like home.
prompts.practice: Close your eyes and smell or hear it in memory.

prompts.prompt: What element—earth, water, fire, air—speaks to you most right now?
prompts.practice: Draw its symbol or name it 3 times.

prompts.prompt: How do you notice the forest/river/sky communicating with you?
prompts.practice: Pause and listen to surrounding sounds for 30 seconds.

prompts.prompt: What small act of care can you offer the earth today?
prompts.practice: Decide one small action (pick up trash, water a plant).

prompts.prompt: How has silence or stillness become part of your medicine?
prompts.practice: Sit in silence for 1 minute before writing.

prompts.prompt: What ritual helps you feel connected to something larger?
prompts.practice: Light a candle or incense if available.

prompts.prompt: Write about a moment when you felt completely interconnected.
prompts.practice: Spread your arms wide, then hug yourself gently.

prompts.prompt: How do you sense the invisible world supporting you now?
prompts.practice: Close your eyes and feel a hand at your back.

prompts.prompt: Where do you find beauty that restores your spirit?
prompts.practice: Look at one object nearby as if seeing it for the first time.

prompts.prompt: What symbolic image from ceremony still guides you?
prompts.practice: Sketch it briefly before journaling.

prompts.prompt: What vision for your life feels aligned with the greater web of existence?
prompts.practice: Write one word that feels like your guiding thread.

prompts.prompt: “When I let go of what I am, I become what I might be.” (Laozi) — What are you ready to release?
prompts.practice: Exhale deeply, imagining release.

prompts.prompt: “The wound is the place where the Light enters you.” (Rumi) — Which wound is now becoming a doorway?
prompts.practice: Place your hand on that part of your body and breathe light in.

prompts.prompt: “He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.” (Nietzsche) — What is your ‘why’ right now?
prompts.practice: Write one sentence that begins with “My why is…”

prompts.prompt: “Our hearts are restless until they rest in You.” (St. Augustine) — Where do you find true rest?
prompts.practice: Sit back, close your eyes, and sigh once deeply.

prompts.prompt: “Silence is the language of God.” (Rumi) — What does silence teach you today?
prompts.practice: Sit in silence for 2 minutes before writing.

prompts.prompt: “Nature does not hurry, yet everything is accomplished.” (Laozi) — Where in your life can you move slower?
prompts.practice: Write one task and cross it out. Let it go.

prompts.prompt: “One must still have chaos in oneself to give birth to a dancing star.” (Nietzsche) — What star is being born in your chaos?
prompts.practice: Draw a tiny star next to your writing.

prompts.prompt: “The soul is healed by being with children.” (Dostoevsky) — How can innocence or play restore you?
prompts.practice: Write with your non-dominant hand for 1 sentence.

prompts.prompt: “God is at home, it is we who have gone out for a walk.” (Meister Eckhart) — Where do you feel most at home in Spirit?
prompts.practice: Close your eyes and imagine that place for 30 seconds.

prompts.prompt: “Stop acting so small. You are the universe in ecstatic motion.” (Rumi) — In what ways can you expand today?
prompts.practice: Stretch your arms wide before writing.

prompts.prompt: “The Tao is like water; it nourishes all things without striving.” (Laozi) — How can you embody water in your life?
prompts.practice: Take a slow sip of water and notice its flow.

prompts.prompt: “Faith is to believe what you do not see; the reward is to see what you believe.” (St. Augustine) — What unseen truth are you trusting?
prompts.practice: Write the word “trust” at the top of your page.

prompts.prompt: Looking back, what has changed most since you began this journaling practice?
prompts.practice: Re-read your first entry before writing today.

prompts.prompt: Which themes or lessons keep repeating for you?
prompts.practice: Circle 3 recurring words from your past entries.

prompts.prompt: What parts of yourself have you welcomed home?
prompts.practice: Write your name slowly, then underline it with care.

prompts.prompt: What integration practices (movement, breath, journaling, service) work best for you?
prompts.practice: Put a star next to the practice you want to keep.

prompts.prompt: What commitment do you want to carry forward into daily life?
prompts.practice: Write it as a promise beginning with “I commit to…”
